title: The largest removable edge sets of the pinched Sierpinski gasket
scope: For every n >= 2: the largest removable edge sets of the pinched Sierpinski gasket have 2^(n-1)+1 edges and are exactly Stappers' 2^(n-1) sets; closed forms for all 15 corner profiles.
gate_basis: gasket_check.py (Python standard library): the profile DP up to n = 24, closure of the profile set, the closed forms, the induction step, the maximizing triples at every step; reconstruction of all largest sets for n <= 10 compared with Stappers' sets built literally from the book's description; comparison with direct colouring and exhaustive search for n = 2, 3. A C colourer cross-check (n <= 5) is logged. One independent AI referee pass.
dependencies: A C compiler for color3.c used by evidence/search/xcheck.py.
limitations: Not externally peer reviewed. Checks so far: the stand-alone program, a separate C colourer, and one independent AI referee pass on 2026-11-17. One independent AI referee (another agent) rebuilt the graphs, a SAT colourability test and the recursion from the text alone, found by exhaustive search the largest removable sets for n = 2..5 (3, 5, 9, 17 edges; 2, 4, 8, 16 sets, equal to Stappers' sets), checked the induction step exactly, and found no mathematical gap; its wording corrections were made.

Computer-assisted. The closed forms for the 15 profiles are proved by induction; the induction step is a finite computation (15^3 triples, explicit thresholds, polynomial identities) done by the program; the profile recursion is checked against direct colouring of the explicit graph.

Knuth's exercise and answer are paraphrased from Pre-Fascicle 7A (5 December 2024), the frozen draft of Volume 4 Fascicle 7, fetched from the Internet Archive; they are cited, not reproduced. Novelty was checked only against that answer.
